BILLAPPA, J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:-
JUDGMENT
The appellants have called in question, the order dated 03.07.2012, passed by the learned Single Judge in W.P.No.64280/2012.

2. By the impugned order, the learned Single Judge has dismissed the writ petition holding that the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 ( 'PFA Act' for short) has been repealed by virtue of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 ('FSS Act, 2006' for short).

Under Section 97 of the FSS Act,
2006, the proceedings are saved.
3.
Aggrieved by that, the appellants have filed this appeal.

4. Briefly stated, the facts are:
The first respondent visited the shop of the first appellant on 29.01.2011 and collected samples of coriander.
Thereafter, a private complaint has been lodged on 11.07.2011 by the first respondent against the appellants.
Cognizance has been taken and summons having been issued to the appellants.
The appellants have appeared before the trial Court on 16.05.2012.
Thereafter, the appellants have approached this Court in W.P.No.64280/2012 seeking to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.991/2011.

The learned Single Judge has dismissed the writ petition holding that the PFA Act,
1954 has been repealed with effect from 05.08.2011 and the proceedings are saved under Section 97 of the FSS Act, 2006.

5. The learned counsel for the appellants contended that Sections 94 to 98 of the FSS Act, 2006 have come into force with effect from July 2010 and therefore, the provisions of PFA Act, 1954 stood repealed and therefore, the proceedings are vitiated in law and the learned Single Judge was not justified in dismissing the writ petition.

sentences.text: As against this, the learned AGA submitted that Sections 94 to 98 of the FSS Act, 2006 have come into force with effect from July 2010 and thereafter, PFA Act, 1954 has been repealed with effect from 05.08.2011.
The complaint has been lodged on 11.07.2011.
Therefore, the proceedings are saved under Section 97 of the FSS Act, 2006.
7. We find considerable force in the submission of the learned AGA.
The complaint has been lodged on 11.07.2011.
Sections 94 to 98 of FSS Act, 2006 have come into force with effect from July 2010.
The PFA Act, 1954 has been repealed with effect from 05.08.2011.

As on the date of complaint, i.e.,
11.07.2011, the provisions of PFA Act, 1954 was in force.
Therefore, the proceedings are saved under Section 97 of the FSS Act, 2006.
The learned Single Judge has rightly dismissed the writ petition.
Therefore, the impugned order does not call for interference.
There is no merit in the appeal and therefore, it is liable to be dismissed.
Accordingly, the writ appeal is dismissed.
